newsitem.title: USA: Second Milwaukee stadium bill in works.
newsitem.headline: Second Milwaukee stadium bill in works.

text.p: Another bill that would limit the amount of tax revenues used to help finance a new $250 million ballpark for the Milwaukee Brewers baseball team is being drafted, the sponsor of the measure in the Wisconsin Senate said Wednesday.
State Sen. Joe Wineke, D-Verona, said his measure would be similar to one proposed last week by Senate Republican Leader Michael Ellis, who yet to introduce his bill.

Wineke said his bill would require the Brewers to pay for any cost overruns at the covertible-roofed ballpark and would prohibit the state-created board overseeing the project from issuing more than $160 million of debt for the project.

The Southeast Wisconsin Professional Baseball Park District Board has so far only sold $146.7 million of convertible option bonds in December, which the district plans to remarket as long-term, fixed-rate debt early next month. The bond are payable with revenues from a five-county, 0.1 percent sales tax.
Wineke said he feared the district would start issuing lease debt to pay for stadium equipment.
"They could be leasing toilet seats," he said.

Under a Wisconsin law that created the district, its board can issue an unlimited amount of debt for the project as long as no more than $160 million of the debt is backed by the state's moral obligation pledge. Neither the December deal nor its upcoming remarketing included that pledge. Instead the issues relied on enhancement from a guarenteed investment contract or bond insurance.

Wineke said his legislation, which he termed a "truth in packaging bill," could be introduced as soon as next week. He also expressed confidence the measure would attract support in the Democrat-controlled Senate.

Michael Duckett, executive director of the district, has said that placing constraints on the board could end up costing taxpayers more money by eliminating future financing options for the stadium and its equipment.

Rating agency officials have said the presence of such a bill would not impact underlying ratings for the upcoming bond issue. The district has a committment from MBIA Insurance Corp. to insure the bonds.
